excimer-laser-for-stretch-marks.summary: A 308 nm UV laser from dermatology, tried on white stretch marks to restore pigment so they blend into surrounding skin.

quick.overview:
The excimer laser is a 308 nm ultraviolet device used in dermatology for vitiligo and psoriasis. On stretch marks that have faded to white, the goal is to bring color back so the marks blend with the skin around them.

The UV light is meant to stimulate pigment-producing cells in the pale marks so they darken toward the surrounding skin tone. Research so far is a small registered phase 1 trial of 10 people with white striae, with no results listed yet.
quick.how: It is a clinic treatment delivered in short sessions, with the laser passed over the pale marks. People usually look at it for mature white stretch marks that have not responded to creams, and results are judged over a series of visits as pigment returns gradually.
quick.risks: Safety data for this specific use were not found. As with other ultraviolet treatments, clinicians weigh sun-exposure and skin-type considerations, so it is delivered by a dermatology provider.

angle.text: The 308 nm excimer laser, used in dermatology for vitiligo and psoriasis, is aimed at white stretch marks to restore pigment so they blend into the surrounding skin. Pigment returns gradually over sessions, and a 10-person early-phase trial has studied it.

prp-for-stretch-marks.summary: Concentrated platelets from your own blood, applied or injected to soften the look of stretch marks, often alongside microneedling or lasers.

quick.overview:
PRP (platelet-rich plasma) is made from your own blood and aims to make stretch marks smoother and less visible.

Platelet growth factors are proposed to drive collagen remodelling and tissue repair in the skin. Research consists of small registered trials, several of which pair PRP with microneedling, fractional lasers or fat grafting, so PRP's own contribution is hard to separate.
quick.how: A small blood sample is spun down to concentrate platelets, and the product is applied to or injected into the marks, frequently after microneedling or laser. People typically do a series of sessions spaced weeks apart and judge texture changes over months.
quick.risks: It is a blood-derived injectable procedure done by clinicians, so the usual considerations of injections apply, such as soreness, bruising and infection risk. No safety data from the registered stretch mark trials were reviewed.

angle.text: Concentrated platelets from your own blood are applied or injected, often with microneedling or lasers, to make stretch marks smoother. Proponents point to growth factors driving collagen remodelling, and small trials have tested it mostly as an add-on.

subcision-tca-cross.summary: A needle procedure that cuts the fibres tethering rolling acne scars so they lift, plus a related acid-based scar technique.

quick.overview:
Subcision releases depressed acne scars so the skin surface looks smoother. TCA CROSS is a separate acid-based procedure often mentioned alongside it for scars.

A needle under the skin cuts the fibrous bands holding a scar down, letting it rise, and the wound-healing response adds collagen. Subcision was described in 1995, and dermatology reviews treat it as one part of combined scar care, supported by small case series and registered trials.
quick.how: Clinicians use it mainly on rolling acne scars, often when other treatments have not lifted tethered scars. It is commonly combined with other scar treatments, and improvement develops over weeks as healing proceeds. Forum accounts of self-performed versions exist, but it is a clinic procedure.
quick.risks: Bleeding, bruising and infection are possible, and clinical guidance lists bleeding disorders, infection and keloid tendency as reasons to avoid it. Limited complication data were found in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: Subcision cuts the fibres tethering rolling acne scars so the depressed skin lifts and new collagen forms, giving a smoother surface. TCA CROSS is a related acid-based scar technique, and small studies and reviews describe subcision as part of combined care.

cortisone-injections-for-keloids.summary: A clinic-given steroid injection into raised keloid scars to flatten and soften them, a long-standing standard now compared with newer agents.

quick.overview:
A clinician injects a corticosteroid, usually triamcinolone, directly into a keloid to flatten it and ease itching, aiming for a flatter, softer scar.

The steroid is described as reducing inflammation and fibroblast activity in the scar. Wikipedia lists it among standard keloid options, introduced in the mid-1960s, and current registered trials compare it with fluorouracil, metformin, lasers and botulinum toxin.
quick.how: It is given in repeated clinic visits over time and is sometimes combined with 5-fluorouracil and pulsed dye laser in adults. Keloids often follow piercings, especially of the earlobes, and are most common between ages 10 and 20.
quick.risks: It is a prescription procedure done by clinicians. A published case report describes a reaction after an injection of triamcinolone with lidocaine, and systematic adverse-event data were not in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: A clinician injects steroid, often triamcinolone, into a raised keloid to reduce inflammation and fibroblast activity so the scar flattens and softens. It is a long-standing option now being compared with newer agents in small trials.

keloid-surgery-radiation.summary: Cutting out a keloid and radiating the wound bed to keep it from regrowing, a clinical standard for severe cases.

quick.overview:
The keloid is surgically removed, so the raised scar is gone right away, and the wound is then treated with radiation to keep it from growing back.

Wikipedia reports recurrence of 70 to 100 percent after excision alone, and lower recurrence when radiation, pressure therapy or laser is added. Published studies describe surgery plus radiotherapy as a standard approach for severe keloids, and one 2020 paper calls radiotherapy essential for preventing recurrence.
quick.how: Radiation is given in the days around the operation as a short course. Researchers also study add-ons such as steroid injection, hyperbaric oxygen, botulinum toxin, photobiomodulation and tension-reducing suturing.
quick.risks: Recurrence, sometimes larger than the original keloid, is the main documented problem. Wikipedia notes radiation is not recommended for children because of the risk of growth abnormalities.

angle.text: Surgical removal takes out the keloid at once, and radiation afterward lowers the chance it regrows, leaving a flat scar. It is a clinical standard for severe cases, since excision alone has high recurrence.

mederma-onion-extract-scar-gel.summary: Over-the-counter onion extract gel applied daily to surgical, burn and acne scars to soften and fade their look.

quick.overview:
Mederma is a widely sold gel containing onion bulb extract, used on surgical, injury, burn and acne scars to make them softer and less visible.

The maker describes moisturizing, cell renewal and collagen support, and onion flavonoids show anti-inflammatory activity in lab studies. Trials include a randomized comparison with a petrolatum emollient on new surgical scars, and results across studies are mixed.
quick.how: People rub a small amount onto healed skin daily, usually for weeks to months, often alongside silicone sheets, massage or sun protection on the scar. Forum posters also try it on old pockmarks.
quick.risks: It is for external use on healed skin, away from eyes and open wounds, per labelling. No serious adverse events are described in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: Users apply this over-the-counter onion extract gel daily to surgical, burn and acne scars so they soften and fade, and some forum posters use it on old pockmarks. Trials against plain emollients have given mixed results.

bio-oil.summary: A popular cosmetic oil used on scars, stretch marks and uneven skin tone to leave skin softer and more supple.

quick.overview:
Bio-Oil is a branded skincare oil used on scars, stretch marks and uneven tone, with the aim of making these areas look softer and smoother.

Its moisturizing oils soften the skin surface. Product-specific trials were not found, and a Cochrane review summarized on Wikipedia found no evidence that creams or oils prevent or reduce stretch marks in pregnancy.
quick.how: People massage it into the area once or twice daily as part of a routine, usually for months, and it is often paired with sun protection on scars.
quick.risks: It is a cosmetic, not a drug, so it is not subject to drug approval. No safety data were found in the sources reviewed, and individual skin reactions to any topical product are possible.

angle.text: Users massage this cosmetic oil into scars, stretch marks and uneven tone so the skin looks softer and more supple. It works as a moisturizer, and product-specific trials were not found.

cocoa-butter-shea-coconut-oil.summary: Plant-fat moisturizers traditionally used to keep skin supple and try to prevent stretch marks, especially in pregnancy.

quick.overview:
Cocoa butter, shea butter and coconut oil are traditional folk choices for keeping skin supple and trying to prevent stretch marks, especially in pregnancy.

They act as emollients that soften and hydrate the skin surface. A registered randomized trial of cocoa butter in pregnancy exists, and a Cochrane review summarized on Wikipedia found no evidence that creams or oils prevent or reduce stretch marks.
quick.how: They are rubbed into the belly, hips, thighs or other stretch-prone areas once or twice daily, often through pregnancy or a growth phase, as part of a moisturizing routine.
quick.risks: Sources reviewed describe no specific harms. Individual skin reactions to any topical product are possible.

angle.text: These plant fats are a traditional choice for keeping skin supple and trying to prevent stretch marks, especially in pregnancy. They moisturize the surface, and a Cochrane review found no evidence that creams or oils prevent marks.

folliculitis-shower-hygiene-post-gym-sho.summary: Showering soon after sweating to wash off sweat and bacteria and keep back and chest breakouts down.

quick.overview:
Showering soon after exercise aims to give you fewer breakouts and bumps on the back, chest and shoulders.

The idea is to remove sweat, oil and surface bacteria that can irritate hair follicles. General references on acne mechanica, caused by heat, friction and pressure, suggest showering soon after exercise, though no controlled study was found.
quick.how: People rinse off right after training rather than sitting in sweaty clothes, and change out of the gym clothes. It is usually paired with clean clothing and sometimes a gentle cleanser.
quick.risks: No harms are described. General advice notes that over-washing or harsh cleansers can irritate skin.

angle.text: Showering soon after sweating washes off sweat, oil and bacteria so back and chest follicles are less likely to get irritated, meaning fewer body breakouts. General references on acne mechanica suggest the habit.

loose-cotton-clothing-washing-sheets.summary: Loose, breathable cotton and regularly washed bedding to cut friction and sweat that cause body breakouts.

quick.overview:
Loose cotton clothing and regularly washed sheets aim to reduce friction and trapped sweat, so fewer clogged follicles and body breakouts appear on the back, chest and shoulders.

Acne mechanica arises from friction, heat and pressure, and Wikipedia suggests loose-fitting breathable fabrics such as cotton over synthetics. Clothing friction is also listed as a trigger of folliculitis. No trials of the habit were found.
quick.how: People choose looser, breathable fabrics for daily wear and training and launder sheets and pillowcases on a regular schedule. It is often combined with showering after sweating.
quick.risks: No harms are described.

angle.text: Loose, breathable cotton and regularly washed bedding reduce friction, heat and trapped sweat on the skin, so fewer follicles get clogged and body breakouts show up less. General references on acne mechanica suggest it.

chlorhexidine-antibacterial-body-wash.summary: A hospital antiseptic wash that some people use to calm body folliculitis and get clearer skin on the back and chest.

quick.overview:
Chlorhexidine is an antiseptic used in surgery and hospitals and sold as a skin wash. Some people use it on the back, chest and shoulders to cut bacteria and calm folliculitis bumps for clearer body skin.

It binds bacterial cell walls and disrupts their membranes. Its research comes from surgical and hospital settings, such as Staphylococcus aureus decolonization, and no trial of its use for cosmetic folliculitis was found.
quick.how: It is used as a body wash in the shower and rinsed off, in a routine for areas prone to folliculitis. It is available over the counter in the United States.
quick.risks: Skin irritation and allergic reactions are reported, and contact with the eyes or ears can cause damage, so labelling says to keep it away from them.

angle.text: People wash the back, chest and shoulders with chlorhexidine to lower skin bacteria and calm folliculitis bumps, leaving clearer body skin. It is studied in hospitals for bacterial decolonization.

antibiotics-doxycycline-for-back-acne.summary: A prescription tetracycline antibiotic widely used for inflamed back and body acne, typically in short courses alongside non-antibiotic treatments.

quick.overview:
Doxycycline is a tetracycline-class antibiotic prescribed for moderate to severe inflammatory acne, including on the back and chest, to clear inflamed lesions and reduce the marks they leave.

It blocks bacterial protein synthesis, and anti-inflammatory effects are also thought to contribute, which is why lower sub-antimicrobial doses are used in acne and rosacea. Dermatology guidance cited on Wikipedia describes oral antibiotics as faster-acting than topicals for inflamed lesions.
quick.how: It is a prescription oral course, usually used alongside topical treatments such as benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid, and commonly for cases where topicals alone have not been enough. Guidance generally recommends limiting courses to about three months.
quick.risks: Common effects include nausea, diarrhoea and increased sunburn risk. Pill esophagitis can occur if swallowed with too little fluid, and use with isotretinoin or other retinoids is contraindicated because of intracranial hypertension risk. The US label warns of tooth discoloration during tooth development and pregnancy concerns, and prolonged use is associated with antibiotic-resistant skin bacteria. It is prescription-only in the US and UK.

angle.text: Doxycycline lowers skin bacteria and inflammation, so inflamed back and body acne lesions clear and leave fewer marks. It is a prescribed acne treatment, with guidelines favouring short courses alongside non-antibiotic treatments.

sunless-tan-body-makeup-to-hide-marks.summary: Self-tanner and body makeup that blend stretch marks and scars into surrounding skin for a day or about a week.

quick.overview:
Self-tanner and body makeup reduce the contrast between stretch marks or scars and the skin around them, giving a more even-looking body for beach days, photos or shirtless occasions. The effect is immediate.

Tanners with DHA darken the surface skin chemically, while bronzers and makeup add temporary color that washes off. No controlled studies of these products for hiding stretch marks or scars were found.
quick.how: Makeup and bronzer last hours and wash off, while DHA tanners (typically 3 to 5 percent in products) develop a brown color over hours that fades over about 3 to 10 days. People apply them before events and reapply as the color fades.
quick.risks: A DHA tan does not protect against UV, and sunscreen added to tanners wears off quickly. The FDA approves DHA for external use but not for eyes, lips, mucous membranes or inhalation. Contact dermatitis has been reported, and lab studies have reported DNA damage and free-radical formation, though a 2010 EU scientific committee opinion found spray tanning posed no risk.

angle.text: Self-tanner and body makeup add color so stretch marks and scars blend into the surrounding skin, and the change is visible right away. People apply it before beach days, photos or shirtless occasions, and it lasts from hours to about a week.

dermablend-tattoo-cover.summary: High-coverage camouflage makeup that hides tattoos, scars and discoloration with heavier coverage than foundation.

quick.overview:
Dermablend is a brand of high-coverage camouflage makeup, and tattoo cover products like it hide tattoos, scars, birthmarks, vitiligo patches and bruises on the face or body. The concealing effect shows as soon as it is applied.

Wikipedia describes cosmetic camouflage as creams or powders that hide color or texture irregularities, first developed by plastic surgeons in World War II for burns, and says it may reduce the psychological impact of skin imperfections. No published trials of specific products were found.
quick.how: Opaque, pigment-rich cream or powder is applied over the area to match the surrounding skin tone, often with color-correcting shades such as green to neutralise redness. It lasts until washed off and is reapplied as needed.
quick.risks: As with other cosmetics, ingredients can cause irritation or allergic reactions in some people. The makeup wears off and needs reapplication.

angle.text: Camouflage makeup such as Dermablend covers tattoos, scars, vitiligo patches and bruises with heavier coverage than foundation, so skin looks even from the moment it is applied. It lasts until it is washed off.

scar-tattooing-micropigmentation.summary: Cosmetic tattooing that places skin-toned pigment in scars or pale patches so they blend with the surrounding skin.

quick.overview:
Scar tattooing, or micropigmentation, deposits pigment into scars, pale vitiligo patches or missing structures such as an areola so they look more like the surrounding skin. The color match shows once healed.

It belongs to the broader field of medical tattooing, and published information describes its history and uses, with evidence cited by Wikipedia consisting mainly of patient satisfaction reviews and general reviews of medical tattooing.
quick.how: A tattoo device places pigment in the dermis in a realistic style meant to imitate normal skin color. For scars, people may instead choose a decorative design that covers the area.
quick.risks: General tattoo risks include infection and allergic reactions. Wikipedia notes diabetes can impair wound healing, so timing and location may need care. Pigment is semi-permanent, and matching skin tone can be difficult.

angle.text: Micropigmentation places skin-toned pigment into scars or pale patches so they blend with the surrounding skin, and the match is visible once healed. It is used after surgery and for vitiligo, and appears among scar procedures in looksmaxxing discussions.

stretch-mark-surgery-tummy-tuck.summary: Abdominoplasty removes loose abdominal skin and tightens the muscle, so you get a flatter midsection and lose stretch marks on the removed skin.

quick.overview:
A tummy tuck (abdominoplasty) removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen and tightens the abdominal wall, giving a flatter midsection. Stretch marks lying within the removed skin, mainly below the navel, go with it.

It is usually sought after pregnancy or major weight loss, and is described as mainly cosmetic with some reconstructive benefit for skin folds and muscle separation. Wikipedia and Grokipedia describe it as a contouring operation and do not address stretch marks directly.
quick.how: Under general anesthesia, skin and fat are excised through a hip-to-hip incision above the pubic area, the muscle fascia is tightened and the navel repositioned. Operating time is 2 to 5 hours, and recovery takes weeks to months.
quick.risks: Wikipedia reports complication rates higher than many other cosmetic surgeries, including seroma, hematoma, infection, wound separation, necrosis, thick or widened scars, numbness, blood clots and anesthesia complications. Smoking, obesity and diabetes raise risk, and it leaves a hip-to-hip scar.

angle.text: Abdominoplasty removes loose abdominal skin and fat and tightens the muscle, so the midsection looks flatter and stretch marks on the removed skin go with it. People seek it after pregnancy or major weight loss, and the change is visible after healing.

slow-bulking-slow-growth-to-avoid-stretc.summary: Gaining weight or muscle gradually in the belief that slower growth lowers the chance of stretch marks on shoulders, arms and chest.

quick.overview:
Some lifters and growing teenagers gain size gradually to build a bigger physique with fewer stretch marks on the shoulders, arms and chest.

Stretch marks are dermal scars thought to come from skin stretching quickly, with tearing of the dermis and elevated cortisol, which can reduce collagen and elastin production, also implicated. Wikipedia lists weight gain, growth spurts, pregnancy and bodybuilding as risk factors alongside genetics and hormones. No study has compared different gain rates.
quick.how: People keep a modest, steady calorie surplus and track weight or measurements over months instead of gaining in fast bursts. It is combined with ordinary training and often with moisturizing routines.
quick.risks: Slow bulking carries no particular documented harm. A Cochrane review summarized on Wikipedia found no evidence that creams or oils prevent stretch marks in pregnancy, and no clearly useful treatment exists once they form.

angle.text: Lifters gain size gradually so the skin has more time to adapt, with the goal of fewer stretch marks on shoulders, arms and chest as the physique grows. Rapid growth is a recognised risk factor for stretch marks, though no trial has compared gain rates.

cellulite-lasers-cellfina.summary: Office procedures that cut or heat the bands behind cellulite dimples to smooth thighs and buttocks; Cellfina has 3-year follow-up data.

quick.overview:
Cellfina and laser devices smooth the dimpled surface of cellulite on the thighs and buttocks.

Cellfina is a tissue-stabilized, guided subcision device that mechanically releases the fibrous bands under the skin associated with dimple-type cellulite. A pivotal open-label multicenter study followed patients for three years and reported sustained improvement. Laser and other energy-based devices are a separate group discussed alongside it, with less published data in the sources reviewed.
quick.how: These are minimally invasive in-office procedures, with improvement appearing as the skin heals. Treating clinicians note that the device is best suited to dimple-type cellulite and that patients often label other body features as cellulite.
quick.risks: Patient selection matters, since not every contour concern is dimple-type cellulite. Complication data are not detailed in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: Cellfina releases the fibrous bands under the skin, and laser devices heat the area, so cellulite dimples on the thighs and buttocks soften into a smoother surface. Cellfina has 3-year follow-up data for dimple-type cellulite.

body-shaving-hair-removal-for-skin-textu.summary: Shaving chest, arms, legs or back for a smoother look that shows muscle definition, visible straight away.

quick.overview:
Men shave or remove chest, arm, leg or back hair to look smoother and to show muscle definition more clearly, especially for physique photos and competitions. The change is visible immediately.

It is a style practice in appearance communities rather than a medical treatment, and little research addresses it for skin texture specifically.
quick.how: Razors or trimmers cut hair at the skin surface, so the look is temporary and repeated as hair grows back. Men most often shave facial hair, and some extend it to the chest, abdomen, underarms and legs.
quick.risks: Cuts, razor burn, razor bumps and ingrown hairs are reported. One well-known investigation of an MRSA skin infection outbreak on a college football team identified cosmetic body shaving and turf burns as facilitating factors.

angle.text: Shaving the chest, arms, legs or back gives a smoother look and shows muscle definition more clearly, especially for physique photos and competitions. The result is visible straight away and is treated as a style choice.

brazilian-tan-spray-tan-to-even-skin.summary: A DHA spray tan that evens out skin tone with a bronze color lasting about a week, with no UV exposure.

quick.overview:
A spray tan applies a DHA solution to even out skin tone and give a bronzed look without UV exposure. The color shows within hours, and people use it before events, shoots and competitions.

DHA reacts with amino acids in the dead outer layer of skin to produce a brown color rather than acting as a dye. A 2005 review described DHA as the only sunless tanning ingredient approved by the FDA and spray-on products as delivering the formulation evenly for a full-body tan.
quick.how: The solution is sprayed across the body in a session, and the color develops over hours. It fades over about a week as the outer skin sheds, and people repeat it ahead of events.
quick.risks: The FDA approves DHA for external use only, not for inhalation or mucous membranes. Contact dermatitis and inhalation concerns are reported, and the tan does not protect against UV.

angle.text: A DHA spray tan reacts with the outer skin to give an even bronze color that lasts about a week, with no UV exposure. The color is visible within hours and is used before events, shoots and competitions.
